arxiv-2103-15190.description: Abstract We prove that the clique graph operator k k is divergent on a locally cyclic graph G G (i. e. N G ​ ( v ) N_{G}(v) is a circle) with minimum degree δ ⁡ ( G ) = 6 \delta(G)=6 if and only if G G is 6 6 -regular.

arxiv-2111-09723.title: Coproducts in Categories of q q -Matroids
arxiv-2111-09723.creator: Heide Gluesing-Luerssen, and Benjamin Jany
arxiv-2111-09723.description: Abstract q q -Matroids form the q q -analogue of classical matroids. In this paper we introduce various types of maps between q q -matroids. These maps are not necessarily linear, but they map subspaces to subspaces and respect the q q -matroid structure in certain ways.

arxiv-2307-07670.title: Efficient Adversarial Attacks on Online Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning
arxiv-2307-07670.creator: Guanlin Liu, Lifeng Lai
arxiv-2307-07670.description: Abstract Due to the broad range of applications of multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL), understanding the effects of adversarial attacks against MARL model is essential for the safe applications of this model. Motivated by this, we investigate the impact of adversarial attacks on MARL.

arxiv-2404-18285.title: A review of the accuracy of Direct Numerical Simulation tools for the simulation of non-spherical bubble collapses
arxiv-2404-18285.creator: Mandeep Saini, Lucas Prouvost, Stephane Popinet, Daniel Fuster
arxiv-2404-18285.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Mandeep Saini, Lucas Prouvost, Stephane Popinet, Daniel Fuster. Numerical methods for the simulation of cavitation processes have been developed for more than 50 years. The rich variety of physical phenomena triggered by the collapse of a bubble has several applications in medicine and environmental science but requires the development of sophisticated numerical methods able to capture the presence of sharp interfaces between fluids and solid/elastic materials, the generation of shock waves and the development of non-spherical modes.

arxiv-2411-04664.title: Processing and Decoding Rydberg Decay Error with MBQC
arxiv-2411-04664.creator: Cheng-Cheng Yu, Zi-Han Chen, Yu-Hao Deng, Ming-Cheng Chen, Chao-Yang Lu, Jian-Wei Pan
arxiv-2411-04664.description: Abstract Achieving fault-tolerant quantum computing with neutral atom necessitates careful consideration of the errors inherent to this system. One typical error is the leakage from Rydberg states during the implementation of multi-qubit gates, which may propagate to multiple correlated errors and deteriorate the performance of error correction.

arxiv-2507-11305.title: Off-shell Formalism for Ali-Ilahi’s ADHM Instanton Sigma Model Present Address : Department of Physical Sciences, Physics Division, College of Science, Jazan University, Jazan 45142, Kingdom of Saudi Arabia
arxiv-2507-11305.creator: Abbas Ali, Mohsin Ilahi, P.P. Abdul Salih
arxiv-2507-11305.description: Abstract In this brief note we present the off-shell superspace formalism for Ali-Ilahi’s ( 0 , 4 ) (0,4) supersymmetric ADHM instanton linear sigma model in harmonic superspace. Ali-Ilahi’s model is dual to the ( 0 , 4 ) (0,4) supersymmetric ADHM instanton linear sigma model constructed by Witten in 1995. Instantons, like solitons, are extended field theoretical solutions.

arxiv-2507-15882.title: Document Haystack: A Long Context Multimodal Image/Document Understanding Vision LLM Benchmark
arxiv-2507-15882.creator: Goeric Huybrechts Srikanth Ronanki Sai Muralidhar Jayanthi Jack Fitzgerald Srinivasan Veeravanallur
arxiv-2507-15882.description: Abstract The proliferation of multimodal Large Language Models has significantly advanced the ability to analyze and understand complex data inputs from different modalities. However, the processing of long documents remains under-explored, largely due to a lack of suitable benchmarks. To address this, we introduce Document Haystack 1 1 1 Dataset: https://huggingface.co/datasets/AmazonScience/document-haystack 2 2 2 Code: https://github.

arxiv-2508-10367.title: Contrast Sensitivity Function of Multimodal Vision-Language Models
arxiv-2508-10367.creator: Pablo Hernández-Cámara, Alexandra Gomez-Villa, Jose Manuel Jaén-Lorites, Jorge Vila-Tomás, Jesus Malo, Valero Laparra
arxiv-2508-10367.description: Abstract Abstract Assessing the alignment of multimodal vision-language models (VLMs) with human perception is essential to understand how they perceive low-level visual features. A key characteristic of human vision is the contrast sensitivity function (CSF), which describes sensitivity to spatial frequency at low-contrasts.

arxiv-2509-19611.title: Evaluating Language Translation Models by Playing Telephone
arxiv-2509-19611.creator: Syeda Jannatus Saba, Steven Skiena
arxiv-2509-19611.description: Abstract Our ability to efficiently and accurately evaluate the quality of machine translation systems has been outrun by the effectiveness of current language models—which limits the potential for further improving these models on more challenging tasks like long-form and literary translation.

britannica-1911-vollmar-georg-heinrich-v.title: Vollmar, Georg Heinrich von (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-vollmar-georg-heinrich-v.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-vollmar-georg-heinrich-v.description: Article 'Vollmar, Georg Heinrich von' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 28), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. VOLLMAR, GEORG HEINRICH VON (1850- ), German Socialist, was born at Munich in 1850. He was educated in a school attached to a Benedictine monastery at Augsburg, and in 1865 entered the Bavarian army as a lieutenant in a cavalry regiment. He served in the campaign of 1866, and then entered the papal army as a volunteer.

pmc-10575874.title: Structural insights into the allosteric inhibition of P2X4 receptors
pmc-10575874.creator: Cheng Shen, Yuqing Zhang, Wenwen Cui, Yimeng Zhao, Danqi Sheng, Xinyu Teng, Miaoqing Shao, Muneyoshi Ichikawa, Jin Wang, Motoyuki Hattori
pmc-10575874.description: P2X receptors are ATP-activated cation channels, and the P2X4 subtype plays important roles in the immune system and the central nervous system, particularly in neuropathic pain. Therefore, P2X4 receptors are of increasing interest as potential drug targets. Here, we report the cryo-EM structures of the zebrafish P2X4 receptor in complex with two P2X4 subtype-specific antagonists, BX430 and BAY-1797.

pmc-10665737.title: Isolation, screening, and identification of chitinase-producing bacterial strains from riverbank soils at Ambo, Western Ethiopia
pmc-10665737.creator: Teshome Gudeta Gonfa, Asefa Keneni Negessa, Abebe Olani Bulto
pmc-10665737.description: Chitinases are hydrolytic enzymes that dissolve the glycosidic linkages in chitin. Chitin is a cell wall component of fungi and fund in exoskeleten of worms and arthropods. Chitinase has been applied in agriculture, as a biopesticide for the control of plant fungal infections, in medicine, and in waste management.

pmc-10670429.title: Docosahexaenoic Acid Explains the Unexplained in Visual Transduction
pmc-10670429.creator: Michael A Crawford, Andrew J Sinclair, Yiqun Wang, Walter F Schmidt, C Leigh Broadhurst, Simon C Dyall, Larry Horn, J Thomas Brenna, Mark R Johnson, Antonino Messina, Alessandro Sergi
pmc-10670429.description: In George Wald’s Nobel Prize acceptance speech for “discoveries concerning the primary physiological and chemical visual processes in the eye”, he noted that events after the activation of rhodopsin are too slow to explain visual reception. Photoreceptor membrane phosphoglycerides contain near-saturation amounts of the omega-3 fatty acid docosahexaenoic acid (DHA).

pmc-11510984.title: Deep Neural Network-Based Cigarette Filter Defect Detection System with FPGA Acceleration for Online Recognition
pmc-11510984.creator: Liang Huang, Qiongxia Shen, Chao Jiang, You Yang, Steve Vanlanduit, Andrea Cataldo
pmc-11510984.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). In the cigarette manufacturing industry, machine vision and artificial intelligence algorithms have been employed to improve production efficiency by detecting product defects. However, achieving both high accuracy and real-time defect detection for cigarettes with complex patterns remains a challenge. To address these issues, this study proposes a model based on RESNET18, combined with a feature enhancement algorithm, to improve detection accuracy.

pmc-11643879.title: Fish Oil Consumption: Its Effects on Bone and Blood Parameters of the Ovariectomized Rat Model of Osteopenia
pmc-11643879.creator: Aggeliki Triantafyllou, Pavlos P. Lelovas, Antonis Galanos, Kyriaki Venetsanou, Christina Passali, Anastasia Patsaki, Dimitrios Pitidis, Stavros K. Kourkoulis, Ismene A. Dontas
pmc-11643879.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Background/Objectives: The beneficial effects of ω-3 fatty acids on the cardiovascular system have been observed in many epidemiological studies; however, their effects on the skeleton and in particular on postmenopausal bone loss appear to vary. The present study’s purpose was to investigate the effects of oral fish oil (rich in ω-3 fatty acids) consumption on bone, plasma, and inflammation parameters in the ovariectomized (Ovx) rat model of osteopenia.

pmc-12653334.title: Cardiomyocyte Nuclear Pleomorphism in a Mouse Model of Inherited Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy
pmc-12653334.creator: Jamie R. Johnston, Isabella Leite Coscarella, Carson L. Rose, Yun Shi, Hosna Rastegarpouyani, Karissa M. Dieseldorff Jones, Jennifer M. Le Patourel, Feyikemi Ogunfuwa, Adriano S. Martins, Kathryn M. Crotty, Katherine M. Ward Molla, Tyler R. Reinoso, Taylor L. Waldmann, Jerome Irianto, Yue Julia Wang
pmc-12653334.description: Mutations in genes encoding sarcomeric proteins are a common cause of cardiomyopathy and sudden cardiac death in humans. We evaluated the hypothesis that myofilament dysfunction is coupled to morphological and functional alterations of cardiomyocyte nuclei in a Tnnc1-targeted knock-in (Tnnc1-p.A8V) mouse model of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM).

pmc-12744135.title: Is the Distal Metatarsal Articular Angle Just Metatarsal Pronation? A Weightbearing CT Analysis
pmc-12744135.creator: Arvind Vijapur, Mohammed Shaath, Nick Cullen, Shelain Patel, Matthew Welck, Karan Malhotra
pmc-12744135.description: Research Type:Level 3 - Retrospective cohort study, Case-control study, Meta-analysis of Level 3 studiesIntroduction/Purpose:The distal metatarsal articular angle (DMAA) is a measurement used in the surgical decision making of hallux valgus correction. However, it is difficult to measure on plain radiographs, is subject to projection bias, and its role in pathology is unclear.

pmc-12750488.title: Quality of Drug Clinical Trials in China: A Mixed Methods Research
pmc-12750488.creator: Xiayan Chen, Hongling Chu, Xiaofang Zhang, Huijuan Li, Jiaxue Meng, Yangfeng Wu
pmc-12750488.description: AimThe quality of drug clinical trials is crucial for authorizing new drugs and fostering innovations in clinical practice. This study aimed to report the status, trends, and factors of the quality of drug clinical trials in China.MethodsThis mixed methods study assessed trial quality using quantitative data from public sources and qualitative data from focus groups and interviews with key stakeholders.

pmc-13143061.title: Exploring obscenity in Nigerian Afro-pop music: A sociocultural analysis of Yoruba youth and social norms
pmc-13143061.creator: Oluwatobi Emmanuel Egbowon, Dilan Çiftçi, Ibrahim Adeshola
pmc-13143061.description: Nigerian Afro-pop music is a popular genre that significantly influences Nigerian society and beyond. While Afro-pop promotes Nigerian culture globally, critics argue that its explicit lyrics and provocative music videos negatively impact young individuals, promoting materialism, sexual promiscuity, and drug use. This research focuses on the cultural implications of “vulgar” Afro-pop music among Yoruba youth in Nigeria.

pmc-13166253.title: The influence of contextual factors on the sustainability of the family talk intervention after implementation when a parent of children or youths has a life-threatening illness
pmc-13166253.creator: Ulrica Åsberg, Tina Lundberg, Malin Lövgren, Ingrid Thermaenius, Anette Alvariza, Camilla Udo
pmc-13166253.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). ObjectivesThere is a lack of family-based psychosocial support interventions in palliative care when a parent of children or youths has a life-threatening illness. One intervention that has shown positive effects is the family talk intervention (FTI).

pmc-13219485.title: Age-associated changes in major lymphocyte subsets and sex-specific patterns in healthy Chinese adults
pmc-13219485.creator: Liqin Xiang, Peng Wu, Chengliang Zhu
pmc-13219485.description: To delineate age-associated changes in major lymphocyte subsets in healthy Chinese adults, identify key inflection points, and explore sex-specific patterns. Flow cytometry data of peripheral blood T, B, and NK cell subsets were collected from 6,550 healthy individuals aged 18–96 years at Hubei Provincial People’s Hospital.

pmc-13400386.title: Impact of prior conventional irinotecan use on nanoliposomal irinotecan efficacy in advanced pancreatic cancer: a meta-analysis
pmc-13400386.creator: S Lee, TL Correa, V Birda, K Roshan, ML Peters, AM Modest, M Keko, B Bockorny
pmc-13400386.description: BackgroundNanoliposomal irinotecan (nal-IRI) has become an established therapy for advanced pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), both in the post-gemcitabine setting and, more recently, in the first-line NALIRIFOX regimen. Concerns remain regarding cross-resistance in patients previously exposed to conventional irinotecan. We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis to evaluate the impact of prior irinotecan exposure on outcomes with nal-IRI.

pmc-13430477.title: Walking into the treatment room is not just a workflow: Therapeutic relationship as supportive care in daily radiotherapy
pmc-13430477.creator: Hsiao-Chuan Liu, Ching-Hsueh Cheng, Min-Chuan Chang, Yen-Ting Liu, Chao-Yuan Tu

pmc-13443138.title: The Gut Microbiome and Diet Interact to Dictate Personalized Response to Broccoli Sprout Consumption
pmc-13443138.creator: Alexandra Alexiev, Laura M. Beaver, John A. Bouranis, Carmen P. Wong, Jan F. Stevens, Thomas J. Sharpton, Emily Ho
pmc-13443138.description: Broccoli sprouts produce sulforaphane (SFN), a dietary isothiocyanate with anti‐cancer and anti‐inflammatory properties. Human intervention trials observe large variation in metabolite generation and bioactivity with broccoli sprout consumption across individuals. We hypothesize that interactions between pre‐intervention diet and personalized gut microbiome composition contribute to this variation.

pmc-13571222.title: Randomized Controlled Trial Comparing AI-Generated, Clinician-Edited to Human-Generated After-Visit Summaries
pmc-13571222.creator: Jonah Zaretsky, Christopher Kim, Vincent Major, Benjamin Verplanke, Christopher Sonne, William Robert Small, Priyanka Solanki, Lucille Fenelon, Nilufar Tursunova, Alyssa Gutjahr, Yunan Zhao, Saul Blecker, Jonathan Austrian, Paul Testa, Jonah Feldman
pmc-13571222.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ObjectiveTo test whether AI-generated, clinician-edited after-visit summaries (AVS) are more patient-friendly than clinician-generated AVS, without compromising safety, when implemented in a live inpatient setting.Patients and MethodsPatients discharged from inpatient medicine units between January 22, 2025, and May 23, 2025, were randomized to the intervention arm, which included AI-generated, clinician-edited AVS, or the control arm, which included usual care of clinician-only AVS.

pmc-13572573.title: Corticosteroid Receptor Modulation in the Dorsal Striatum Prevents Morphine‐Induced Place Preference and Reduction in Dopamine Transporter (DAT) Immunoreactivity in Rats
pmc-13572573.creator: Payman Raise‐Abdullahi, Fatemeh Rezamohammadi, Mehrnoush Rahmani, Abbas Ali Vafaei, Roghayeh Pakdel, Hamed Rashidipour, Ali Rashidy‐Pour
pmc-13572573.description: Stress hormones and corticosteroid signalling influence dopaminergic transmission and reward‐related behaviours. The present study investigated whether pharmacological manipulation of corticosteroid signalling within the dorsal striatum influences morphine‐induced conditioned place preference (CPP) and dopamine transporter (DAT) regulation. Male Wistar rats were implanted with bilateral intra‐dorsal striatal cannulae and subjected to the CPP paradigm.
